paper_metadata.title: Simultaneously enhancing room-temperature strength-ductility synergy and high-temperature performance of titanium matrix composites via building a unique bimodal architecture with multi-scale reinforcements

evidence.quote: conventional high-temperature titanium alloys or titanium matrix composites (TMCs) are encountering a huge challenge that the room-temperature ductility will be inevitably deteriorated in pursuit of enhancing the elevated high-temperature strength.

evidence.section: 3.1. Microstructure of the as-sintered (TiB + Y2O3)/Ti composite
evidence.quote: Ti-B-Y mixed powders were sintered at 1300 ◦C/50 MPa/1.5 h to prepare the titanium matrix composite. As shown in Fig. 2 (a), the as-sintered titanium matrix composite exhibited a typical Widmanstatten microstructure consisting of α/β lath clusters and it was found that microsized black rods and white elliptical particles with the size of 100 nm-1 μm (see the inset of Fig. 2 (a)) exhibited a quasi-network distribution along the grain boundary of the Widmanstatten microstructure.
